title: Imagination Engineering: "Live in the future and then build what's missing."
talk_summary: A YC design lead demos personal 'imagination engineering' experiments: dumping stream-of-consciousness into a Slack channel, then having an agent turn it into websites, tools, and MD files. It is mostly inspiration and product demos, not an engineering talk about agent systems.

takeaways.technique: Agent-readable MD glossary of a UI/page
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of making agents read a rendered page, they generate a Markdown glossary of all information displayed, which agents can parse cheaply.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's a glossary of all the information that is displayed on this project. Super easily readable by the agents and it's a lot more efficient than having the agent look at this page

takeaways.technique: Distilled voice/style MD + auto-updated design-language MD
takeaways.what_they_do: They distill a person's writings into a 'voice.md' and the site's design language into an MD that auto-updates whenever a component or design change is made.
takeaways.evidence_quote: whenever I make a a change to the design of this website or create a new uh component, it automatically updates it

takeaways.technique: Personal reusable skills invoked on demand
takeaways.what_they_do: They created a set of personal 'skills' they can invoke at any point in the workflow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I created a few skills for myself that I can in invoke at any given point

takeaways.what_they_do: They start a visible timer when beginning a project to bound how much time to spend and force scope decisions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I made a timer for myself uh when I started 10:10 a.m. so that I knew exactly how much time I had to work on this project

takeaways.what_they_do: They dump every idea into a Slack channel and let an agent aggregate it into a site/backlog, turning idle thoughts into queued work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: whatever stream of consciousness you have, you should just ask an agent to do it for you
